description: Cologne, Germany (Hybrid) Team: Product & Engineering · Reports to: CTO · Format: Full-time, permanent Own a piece of the product, not a ticket queue ilert is the alerting, on-call and incident response platform that engineering teams worldwide rely on when things break. That covers alerting, on-call scheduling, call routing, status pages, and an AI SRE that investigates incidents alongside the people responding to them. We're bootstrapped, profitable, and small (~15 engineers). Your work reaches customers fast, and you have a real say in what gets built. We're looking for a Product Engineer to own one area of that product. We'll give you a domain, not a spec. You figure out what customers need, build it across the stack, ship it, and check whether it made a difference. We build with AI every day. But AI is leverage on top of engineering, not a substitute for it. We're looking for a solid engineer first, someone who uses AI to move faster, not to skip understanding the code. Tasks Own a product domain end-to-end. Depending on where you'll have the most impact, that could be alerting, on-call and call routing, status pages, integrations, or our AI SRE. You propose what to build, build it, and measure whether it worked. Ship across the stack. Java and Rust on the backend, React and TypeScript on the frontend. We work in 2-week bets that end in a production deploy. Talk to customers. Join customer calls, read support conversations, dig into usage data, and turn what you learn into product improvements. Make the scope calls. Decide what to cut, what ships first, and what to validate before building it. We trust you with these trade-offs. Own it in production. You're responsible for what you ship, including when it breaks. Reliability is literally our product. What you bring 2+ years of software engineering in a team codebase. That means code review, tests, production incidents, and code you didn't write alone. Side projects are great, but they don't replace this. You've shipped features end-to-end and cared whether people actually used them. Comfortable across the stack. Strong on one side, and willing and able to work on the other. Solid fundamentals. Data modeling, debugging, testing, and thinking through failure modes. You can read unfamiliar code and reason about it before you reach for a prompt. Real AI fluency. You use AI coding tools every day, you know where they help and where they mislead, and you can defend a design decision without "the AI suggested it." Product instinct. You have opinions about what to build, not just how . Comfortable with ambiguity. A domain and a problem are enough for you to get going. Fluent English (our working language). title: Product Manager
description: About Nous Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute. We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money. We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked. Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent. And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people". The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build. How we build (worth reading before the role) How products get built is changing fast. With AI tooling, a PM can prototype, dig into production data and commit production code to get a change live all in an afternoon. An engineer can own a product area end to end and decide what to build next. We're leaning into that. Our PMs lean into code and our engineers run products: one of our engineers owns the car insurance targets. We care about whatever gets the job done most effectively, regardless of once upon a time whose job it was meant to be. We're moving fast and adapting as we go, and we don't have all the answers yet. What should a squad look like when everyone can build? Where does process still help, and where does it just slow you down? What's a PM for when an engineer can run the experiment themselves? We're working it out, and we want someone who is excited to be part of helping figure it out. About the role So where does a PM fit? A lot of our work still suits squads: clear targets, a few service lines and a team of engineers. Those squads need product managers to run them. All our roles in product overlap, but this one is centred on product management. If you’d rather spend all your time building, have a look at our Product Builder role. You’ll take a squad responsible for a key section of our product and service lines and grow them: expand what they cover, understand the levers that drive their performance (automation, new suppliers, what we recommend to members) and increase their commercial value. Being a Product Manager at Nous is one of the hardest roles we have. The product is complex and we move fast, so you need to be able to hold a lot of context. You'll switch between very different things all day: thinking about OKRs and the plan for the next couple of weeks one moment, getting a PR into production the next, while helping unblock an engineer. That's also what makes it exciting. You bring order to fast-moving work, get some sequencing in place so people aren’t each figuring it out on their own, evaluate what’s being shipped, own the reporting and keep the squad’s energy up. You won’t hesitate to make changes yourself, but you won’t be just another builder in the squad either: when you’re heads-down building, you can’t unblock anyone or bring the team together. Growing a service line here means working across the boundary between product and commercial, so we’re particularly interested in PMs who’ve had real exposure to the commercial side of a business. Our agent acts in the real world a lot, so saving someone money takes more than great product execution. We also need access to the best tariffs and suppliers, and we have to understand the regulation we operate in. And because Nous is an agent, your nice neat Amplitude funnels don't work: every user's journey can be totally different. So we're after PMs who are excited by everything it takes to make an agentic product work for real households, including the bits that wouldn't traditionally count as "product". Worth being upfront: we can't tell you yet which service lines you'd own. It depends on the Venn diagram of your particular skill set and the problems we need to solve at the point you join. What matters most We need all of these at once: Sharp. You pick things up quickly and enjoy hard problems. Given a messy one, you can lay out what you know and what you'd check first, then change your mind as new data turns up. Adaptable. We’re working a lot of this out as we go, so the role and the squad will change, probably more than once. You enjoy that. You pick up whatever’s needed, PM work or not, and you work in the open: sharing rough thinking early and changing course when someone has a better idea. Delivery. You bring order to a fast-moving squad: clear priorities, sensible sequencing, people unblocked quickly, and an honest look at whether what shipped actually worked. Product craft. You find the real problem behind a request and make the trade-offs explicit. You care about the details of what our users actually see. Commercial and analytical. You know what your area made last month, what moved it and what you'd do next, and you answer most of your own questions with data. You think in conversion, margin and lifetime value as readily as in features. Energy. You've probably worked at a startup. You move fast, you're happy doing the unglamorous work yourself, and you'd rather ship this week's version than polish next quarter's. And everyone builds here, PMs included. You'll use AI tooling (Claude Code or whatever gets it done) to prototype, dig into data and ship changes yourself. You don't need to be an engineer, but you shouldn't be scared of code. What you'll actually do Grow your service lines. Understand what really drives their performance, be able to measure it, and lead the squad to deliver it. Set the squad's OKRs and roadmap, get the sequencing in place, and drive fast, efficient execution. Evaluate what’s being shipped, and own the reporting: make sure the reports and the data behind them make sense. Work across product and commercial: the suppliers and tariffs we can offer, the regulation we work within, and what that means for what gets built. Run experiments, and unblock yourself on the analysis without always needing an analyst. Get close to members and ops. Read the conversations, sit with the people handling the edge cases, and fix the parts of the journey where people drop out or get stuck. About you You'll likely thrive here if: You've been a PM for a few years, ideally at a startup, and you've owned something with a number attached: revenue, conversion, retention. You're comfortable enough with data and code to unblock yourself. Nice-to-haves: You were a software engineer before you moved into product. You've worked on a transactional or regulated product: insurance, fintech, energy, marketplaces. You've built and shipped your own thing: a startup, a side project, an internal tool that took off. This probably isn't for you if your PM experience is mostly roadmaps and stakeholder management at a big company, with no number you owned. How we work We keep the middle thin, on purpose. There's barely any middle management, which means fewer bottlenecks and room for exceptional people to have real impact without first being promoted into managing others. It's a real bet, not a free lunch. Instead of a manager buffer, you get lots of context and colleagues who help because they're invested, not because an org chart says so. If you need a clear remit handed down before you can move, this probably won't suit you. Your first 90 days are built around getting you to real ownership safely: pairing when you want it, lots of context, and people who want you to ship. We celebrate the person who built the unglamorous version this week, not whoever thought of it first. We're office-first, near Farringdon. We do a lot of our best thinking together and being in the same room helps, though we're pragmatic about heads-down work when you need it. title: Software Engineer, Pub/Sub
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>Our everyday digital experiences are in the middle of a realtime revolution: chatting alongside a livestream, getting realtime financial updates, or working with colleagues in a shared online space. Consumers now expect realtime as standard, and Ably powers a large part of it.</p> <p>We put developers first. Our products help teams build, extend, and deliver realtime digital experiences, delivering over 700 billion messages to more than 2 billion devices every month. Teams at HubSpot, Fin, Dialpad, NASCAR, Sportsbet, and General Motors all build on Ably.</p> <p>Working at Ably means helping build the infrastructure that will shape the next generation of the internet. More of what people do online is becoming live, shared and interactive, which only makes what we build more relevant and more necessary. AI is the latest place that shows up. There's still so much to build, and we'd like your help with it.</p></div><h2><strong>About this role</strong></h2> <p>The Pub/Sub team owns the core backend that underpins Ably's entire edge messaging platform. This is a rare opportunity to work on genuinely hard distributed systems problems at planet scale; designing and improving the infrastructure that developers and their users depend on in production every day.</p> <p>You'll be hands-on, driving the development of new functionality and initiatives to scale and improve Ably's core Pub/Sub platform. We work in an AI-first engineering culture: AI tools are part of how we plan, prototype, and iterate - but engineers own every technical decision, and human judgment is the quality bar that everything is measured against.</p> <p>You can read more about the core concepts of working on a truly distributed system in our blog post<a href="https://ably.com/blog/what-is-a-distributed-systems-engineer"> here</a>.</p> <h2><strong>Day to day you will</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Deliver key platform functionality.</strong>&nbsp; You'll work across Ably's realtime products including our low-level Pub/Sub APIs, our LiveObjects state synchronisation layer, and AI Transport, the messaging backbone purpose-built for AI agent communication, focussing on shipping new features, performance improvements, bug fixes and maintenance.</li> <li><strong>Work fluently with AI tooling.</strong> You'll use AI tools for planning, spike work, code generation, and documentation, while taking full ownership of correctness, architectural quality, and what actually ships. Fast iteration is expected; shortcuts in quality are not.</li> <li><strong>Solve hard distributed systems problems</strong>. You'll collaborate with a talented engineering team to work through genuinely interesting and challenging technical problems.</li> <li><strong>Stay driven by 'Developer First' principles</strong>. You'll work closely with other engineers to identify and address the most important problems developers face when building on Ably.</li> <li><strong>Push to see your work in customers' hands</strong>. You'll move with urgency to ship, because you care about the impact your work has on the developers and companies building on our platform.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>We'd love to talk if you have</strong></h2> <ul> <li>A strong interest in, or direct experience with, distributed systems and large-scale infrastructure.</li> <li>Experience working with or building messaging queues, pub/sub systems, or streaming systems at scale.</li> <li>Extensive experience with a high-level server-side language (Node.js or Go preferred).</li> <li>The ability to self-start, work through ambiguity, and make good decisions without a lot of hand-holding.</li> <li>A practical relationship with AI tooling. You use it to go faster and think more clearly, and you know where to apply rigour that AI alone can't provide.</li> <li>A transparent, collaborative 'build in the open' mindset. You're comfortable sharing your work publicly, whether that's writing about what you're building, talking about technical decisions, or contributing to the broader developer conversation around the problems Ably solves.</li> <li>Experience in dynamic, early-stage environments where adaptability and resourcefulness are core skills.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Bonus points if you have</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience building developer-first products.</li> <li>Experience with products brought to market through a product-led growth approach.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><h2><strong>What’s it like to work at Ably?</strong></h2> <p>You'll join a team of around 60 people, working directly alongside senior engineering and leadership. No layers, no bureaucracy, and real ownership from day one.</p> <h3>Remote-first</h3> <p>We hire the best people wherever they are across the UK and Europe, trust them to own their work, and share decisions and feedback openly. Twice a year, in February and August, we all meet in person, and we expect everyone to be there.</p> <p>Remote-first comes with trade-offs. On one side: flexibility, no commute, long stretches of focus time, and a wider pool of people to hire from. On the other: it can feel isolating, relationships take effort to build, and you miss the chance conversations an office creates. As our only recruiter, you'll need to manage your own time and stay close to the hiring managers and candidates you work with.</p> <p>If you do your best work with trust and autonomy, this will suit you. If you'd rather have an office around you every day, it probably isn't the right fit.</p> <p>Our six values shape how we work day to day:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Open for all.</strong> We default to sharing openly: source, decisions, and feedback, with open minds to match.</li> <li><strong>Tech needs humanity.</strong> We build with empathy, for colleagues and developers alike.</li> <li><strong>Even the best do better.</strong> We keep raising our own bar, driven by curiosity, not complacency.</li> <li><strong>Bias for action.</strong> Once we know enough to act, we act, rather than waiting for certainty.</li> <li><strong>Dependable by default.</strong> We take real ownership of what we ship and what we promise.</li> <li><strong>Bold creativity wins.</strong> We treat big constraints as a reason to think differently, not less.</li> </ul> <p>You can read more about how we defined these values on <a href="ably.com/blog/ably-values">our blog</a>, and see the team behind them on our&nbsp;<a href="ably.com/careers">careers page</a>.</p> <h2>Diversity, inclusion, and belonging at Ably</h2> <p>We believe our differences as individuals are what make us great. Our people are at the heart of what we do, and we encourage everyone to be their most authentic self at Ably: we see inclusivity and openness as fundamental to our long-term success. We encourage applications from all backgrounds regardless of age, disability, gender, sexual orientation, parental status, race, religion, educational background, or neurodiversity. Ably has an amazing opportunity ahead of us, and we want anyone to be able to contribute to it.</p> <p><em>If you enjoy working as part of a technology company, value open source, and love solving hard problems, we'd love to hear from you, regardless of whether you fit the job description exactly or not. If in doubt, drop us an&nbsp;<span style="font-weight: 400;"><a ----- target="_blank">email</a>;</span>; we're happy to give you advice on your application.</em></p> <h2>What you'll get</h2> <ul> <li>A remote-first and flexible work environment. Our London office (next to Old Street) is there whenever you want it. Aside from our company get-togethers, you're welcome to work wherever suits you best.</li> <li>Equity. We're a growing start-up, and we want everyone to share in the company's success through our EMI share options programme.</li> <li>Enhanced holiday allowance: 28 days of paid annual leave (27 regular days, plus a day off to enjoy your birthday).</li> <li>Enhanced parental leave, so you can spend time with your new family member: up to 16 weeks fully paid for primary caregivers and 4 weeks for secondary, depending on length of service.&nbsp;</li> <li>A home workstation budget of £500 on joining (and £150 per year after that), so your home office serves you well.</li> <li>A personal learning and development budget of £1000 a year, plus 5% L&amp;D time during working hours to build your skills.</li> <li>Private healthcare with BUPA.</li> <li>A medical cash plan covering a range of medical and dental costs.</li> <li>Mental wellbeing coaching and counselling from Self Space.</li> <li>A monthly wellbeing budget via Juno.</li> <li>Life assurance and income protection.</li> <li>Access to Tech and Cycle to Work schemes.</li> <li>A weekly snack allowance for our end-of-week "Need to Know" meeting.</li> <li>A fully-paid one-month sabbatical after five years with Ably.</li> </ul></div> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow
